name: Stored Data Manipulation
summary: Adversaries may insert, delete, or manipulate data at rest in order to influence external outcomes or hide activity, thus threatening the integrity of the data. By manipulating stored data, adversaries may attempt to affect a business process, organizational understanding, and decision making. strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Stored Data Manipulation across OS Platforms.

analytics.name: Analytic 0555
analytics.guidance: Identify unauthorized creation, deletion, or modification of business-critical stored data such as Office documents, database files, and log archives. Detect anomalous processes modifying stored data outside of expected workflows (e.g., non-database processes modifying database files).

analytics.name: Analytic 0556
analytics.guidance: Detect suspicious file creation, modification, or deletion in stored data directories (e.g., `/var/lib/mysql/`, `/var/log/`, mail spools). Identify shell commands interacting directly with structured data files instead of legitimate database utilities.

analytics.name: Analytic 0557
analytics.guidance: Monitor sensitive data files such as plist-based storage, mail archives, or Office files for unexpected modifications. Detect anomalous processes modifying stored data outside expected update cycles using FSEvents and Unified Logs.
